title: Previous-year melt did not change the next summer balance of 233 WGMS glaciers in 1951-2023 with Berkeley Earth temperature; GHCN-CAMS temperature gives false lag terms
abstract: Question: does a year with strong melt make the next summer's melt larger than the next summer's weather explains (memory from firn loss and darker ice)? We used 4,251 glacier-years of measured summer and winter balance from 233 glaciers in the WGMS Fluctuations of Glaciers database (2026-02-10). We used summer air temperature at each glacier from Berkeley Earth. The models had glacier and year fixed effects and two-way clustered errors. Same-summer temperature gave -0.49 m w.e. per deg C. Previous-summer temperature gave +0.029 (95% CI -0.010 to +0.068), and memory predicts a negative value. Next-summer temperature (placebo) gave -0.005. Previous-year annual balance gave +0.002 m w.e. per m w.e. (CI -0.049 to +0.053), with the same result in 7 specifications. After a glacier's lowest-decile year (residual -0.41 m w.e.), the next-year residual was +0.001 (CI -0.06 to +0.06; 495 events). With training on 1951-2005 and testing on 2006-2024, lagged terms did not decrease the forecast error. The Alps in 2023 had a residual of -0.22 m w.e. after 2022, but this is one regional case. The planned GHCN-CAMS analysis failed its placebo test: previous-summer and next-summer temperature both gave about +0.09 to +0.10. GHCN-CAMS summer balance responded 3 to 4 times less to multi-year temperature than to year-to-year temperature, and Berkeley Earth did not show this difference. A GHCN-CAMS model also predicted 0.35 m w.e. per year too little loss in 2006-2025. Limitations: the temperature is from coarse grid cells, the models have no radiation or summer snowfall terms, some national series are model-based, and memory through thinning over decades is not tested.

display.caption: Summer balance residual (same-year Berkeley Earth summer temperature and winter balance removed; glacier and year fixed effects) from 3 years before to 3 years after each glacier's lowest-decile (detrended) annual balance year. Mean and 95% CI clustered by event year; 495 events, 1951-2024. The residual is back at 0 one year after the extreme year.

Coefficients of previous-summer temperature (test; memory predicts a negative value) and next-summer temperature (placebo) on summer balance, across 7 specifications, for Berkeley Earth (left) and GHCN-CAMS (right) temperature. 95% CI, two-way clustered. With Berkeley Earth, both are near 0. With GHCN-CAMS, both are positive and equal, so the placebo test fails.

Summer balance response to the year-to-year part and the multi-year (centred 3-, 5- and 7-year mean) part of summer temperature, on the same glacier-years. GHCN-CAMS gives a 3-4 times weaker multi-year response. Berkeley Earth gives almost equal responses.

Berkeley Earth gridded land temperature (Complete_TAVG_LatLong1) is the main temperature input.
GHCN-CAMS monthly land temperature is the planned temperature input. We show that its multi-year variability gives false lag and lead terms for glacier balance.
